distractors.reason: 'Big' describes size, not the quality of a diet. We don't say 'big diet' to mean a good way of eating.
'Fast' describes speed. 'Fast food' is a fixed phrase, but 'fast diet' does not mean a healthy way of eating.
'Strong' describes intensity, such as strong coffee. We don't say 'strong diet' for a healthy way of eating.

example_sentence: Eating fruit and vegetables is part of a ___ diet.
l1_interference: Los hispanohablantes pueden usar 'strong' porque en español se dice 'comida fuerte' para algo consistente. En inglés, para una alimentación sana, se dice 'healthy diet'.
explanation: In English, 'healthy' is the normal adjective for food and diets that are good for your body. Learn 'healthy diet' as one fixed phrase.

related_collocations.example: I ate a heavy meal, so I feel tired.

memory_tip: HEALTHY = good for your body (healthy diet, healthy food) | BIG/STRONG/FAST describe size, intensity or speed, not health
